Commands are are used to store and retrieve data. Each types has different sets of commands.

Some other common data types in redis are: string, list, hash, set, sorted set, bitmap, hyperlog, JSON, and index

For example Strings:
- SET key value
- GET key

// Set key value
SET message 'Hi There'

// Get a value by key
GET message

## Redis `SET` Syntax

```text
SET key value
    [ NX
    | XX
    | IFEQ ifeq-value
    | IFNE ifne-value
    | IFDEQ ifdeq-digest
    | IFDNE ifdne-digest
    ]
    [ GET ]
    [
      EX seconds
    | PX milliseconds
    | EXAT unix-time-seconds
    | PXAT unix-time-milliseconds
    | KEEPTTL
    ]
```

 Syntax Notation:

- UPPERCASE = keyword you type as shown.
- lowercase = placeholder; replace it with your value.
- [] = optional; you can omit it.
- | = OR; choose one alternative.
- "" = quotes; group text into a single string when needed.

key value = required arguments.

Important:

- key, value, seconds, milliseconds, ifeq-value, and ifeq-digest are placeholders, not literal keywords.
- NX, XX, GET, EX, PX, EXAT, PXAT, and KEEPTTL are options you type literally.
- The square brackets and vertical bars in the syntax diagram are documentation notation. Do not type them into the Redis command.
- The options have specific rules; you cannot freely combine every option with every other option.
- [ | ] - if you see | , only one option can be selected.
